data.narrative:
Blue Water Autonomy is a Series A defense and security company founded by Rylan Hamilton and Austin Gray that has raised $64M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms, including Stark Defence, Singularity, NODA AI, Anduril Industries, and Helsing.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $64M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $128M. Peer-median analysis across 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables produces a median of $400M, with the peer set ranging from $125M (NODA AI) to $4.0B (Stark Defence). The disparity reflects sector and company-specific factors.

Triangulating these two approaches produces a valuation range of $109M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $264M. The wide spread reflects meaningful uncertainty in peer selection within the Defense & Security sector at Series A, where valuations span two orders of magnitude. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to actual capital deployed; the peer-median method captures market pricing but is sensitive to which comparables are weighted. Capital efficiency and technology differentiation relative to the peer set represent key unresolved valuation drivers.
